00257|           env: process.env,
00258|           encoding: 'utf8',
00259|           maxBuffer: 64 * 1024 * 1024,

00265|         // Leave observedModel undefined.
00266|       }
00267|     }
00268|   }

00270| 
00271|   if (res.error || agentExitCode !== 0) {
00272|     // Mirror the old error string: last 5 lines of output, else a coded fallback.
00273|     const errorLines = output.trim().split('\n').slice(-5).join('\n');
00274|     const fallback = res.error
00275|       ? `Failed to run opencode: ${res.error.message}`
00276|       : `OpenCode CLI exited with code ${agentExitCode}`;
00277|     return {
00278|       ok: false,
00279|       output,
00280|       transcript,
00281|       observedModel: observedModelOrNull,
00282|       error: errorLines || fallback,
00283|       agentExitCode,
00284|     };
00285|   }
00286| 
00287|   return {
00288|     ok: true,
00289|     output,
00290|     transcript,
00291|     observedModel: observedModelOrNull,
00292|     error: null,
00293|     agentExitCode,
00294|   };
00295| }

00297| /* ─────────────────────────── runnable (CLI) entry ─────────────────────────── */
00298|

00300| const isMain = process.argv[1] && fileURLToPath(import.meta.url) === process.argv[1];

00302| if (isMain) {

00304|   const input = JSON.parse(process.argv[2]);

00307|   // always has a result file to read (node exit code stays 0 except on a truly
00308|   // unrecoverable crash before we can write).
00309|   let result;
00310|   try {
00311|     result = await runAgent(input);
00312|   } catch (e) {
00313|     result = {
00314|       ok: false,
00315|       output: '',
00316|       transcript: null,
00317|       observedModel: null,
00318|       error: e && e.message ? e.message : String(e),
00319|       agentExitCode: -1,
00320|     };
00321|   }
00322|

00324|   try {
00325|     mkdirSync(dirname(input.resultPath), { recursive: true });
00326|     writeFileSync(input.resultPath, JSON.stringify(result));
00327|   } catch {
00328|     // If the file can't be written, the host falls back to the marker line below.
00329|   }
00330| 
00331|   // Fallback channel: a compact status line (no transcript — it can be huge).
00332|   process.stdout.write(
00333|     '__AGENT_RESULT__ ' +
00334|       JSON.stringify({
00335|         ok: result.ok,
00336|         observedModel: result.observedModel,
00337|         error: result.error,
00338|         agentExitCode: result.agentExitCode,
00339|       }) +
00340|       '\n'
00341|   );
00342| 
00343|   // Exit 0: "the runner ran". Agent success/failure is conveyed via result.ok, not
00344|   // the node exit code (the host distinguishes the two).
00345|   process.exit(0);
00346| }

/**
 * OpenCode in-sandbox runner.
 *
 * This file is shipped INTO the sandbox by the orchestrator and executed there as
 * `node __agent_eval__/run.mjs '<AgentRunInput JSON>'`. It is intentionally
 * ZERO-DEPENDENCY (only `node:*` builtins) because the sandbox only has the
 * fixture's own deps + the installed `opencode` CLI — it cannot import anything
 * from the @vercel/agent-eval package.
 *
 * Dual mode:
 *   - runnable: invoked directly → reads argv, runs the agent, writes the result
 *     file + prints a status line, exits 0.
 *   - importable: `import { runAgent } from './run.mjs'` → returns a RunnerResult
 *     (no file write, no exit). This is what a future in-sandbox judge reuses.
 *
 * The pure helpers below are exported (not just `runAgent`) so they can be
 * unit-tested directly — the same code the sandbox runs (see opencode.test.ts).
 */

import { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';

<file>
00002| title: How to set up your Next.js project for AI coding agents
00003| nav_title: AI Coding Agents
00004| description: Learn how to configure your Next.js project so AI coding agents use up-to-date documentation instead of outdated training data.
00005| related:
00006|   title: Next Steps
00007|   links:
00008|     - app/guides/mcp
00009|     - app/getting-started/upgrading
00010|     - app/api-reference/cli/create-next-app
00011|     - app/api-reference/cli/next
00012| ---
00013| 
00014| Next.js ships version-matched documentation inside the `next` package, allowing AI coding agents to reference accurate, up-to-date APIs and patterns. An `AGENTS.md` file at the root of your project directs agents to these bundled docs instead of their training data.
00015| 
00016| Point agents at the bundled docs, give them [runtime visibility](#step-2-give-agents-runtime-visibility) into the dev server, let [errors drive the fixes](#step-3-let-errors-drive-the-fixes), and hand multi-step workflows to [skills](#step-4-hand-multi-step-workflows-to-skills).
00017| 
00018| ## Step 1: Point agents at the bundled docs
00019| 
00020| Make sure `AGENTS.md` exists at your project root and directs agents to the bundled docs. When you install `next`, the Next.js documentation is bundled at `node_modules/next/dist/docs/`, mirroring the structure of the [Next.js documentation site](https://nextjs.org/docs):
00021| 
00022| ```txt
00023| node_modules/next/dist/docs/
00024| ├── 01-app/
00025| │   ├── 01-getting-started/
00026| │   ├── 02-guides/
00027| │   └── 03-api-reference/
00028| ├── 02-pages/
00029| ├── 03-architecture/
00030| └── index.mdx
00031| ```
00032| 
00033| Agents always have access to docs that match your installed version, with no network request or external lookup required. [Upgrading Next.js](/docs/app/getting-started/upgrading) also upgrades the bundled docs, including new guidance for existing features. Most AI coding agents, including Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and GitHub Copilot, automatically read `AGENTS.md` when they start a session.
00034| 
00035| ### New projects
00036| 
00037| [`create-next-app`](/docs/app/api-reference/cli/create-next-app) generates `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` automatically. No additional setup is needed:
00038| 
00039| ```bash package="pnpm"
00040| pnpm create next-app@canary
00041| ```
00042| 
00043| ```bash package="npm"
00044| npx create-next-app@canary
00045| ```
00046| 
00047| ```bash package="yarn"
00048| yarn create next-app@canary
00049| ```
00050| 
00051| ```bash package="bun"
00052| bun create next-app@canary
00053| ```
00054| 
00055| If you don't want the agent files, pass `--no-agents-md`:
00056| 
00057| ```bash
00058| npx create-next-app@canary --no-agents-md
00059| ```
00060| 
00061| ### Existing projects
00062| 
00063| On Next.js 16.3 or later, run `next dev`. When an AI coding agent is detected in the environment and no managed block is present, Next.js auto-generates `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` at the project root. Existing `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md` files are upserted, so content outside the managed block is preserved:
00064| 
00065| ```md filename="AGENTS.md"
00066| <!-- BEGIN:nextjs-agent-rules -->
00067| 
00068| # This is NOT the Next.js you know
00069| 
00070| This version has breaking changes — APIs, conventions, and file structure may all differ from your training data. Read the relevant guide in `node_modules/next/dist/docs/` (resolved from this file's directory; in monorepos the `next` package may not be visible from the repo root) before writing any code. Heed deprecation notices.
00071| 
00072| This block is written and re-added by `next dev` — verify at `node_modules/next/dist/server/lib/generate-agent-files.js`. Removing it from a diff only re-creates the uncommitted change; committing it with your work keeps the tree clean.
00073| 
00074| <!-- END:nextjs-agent-rules -->
00075| ```
00076| 
00077| ```md filename="CLAUDE.md"
00078| @AGENTS.md
00079| ```
00080| 
00081| Add your own project-specific instructions outside the `<!-- BEGIN:nextjs-agent-rules -->` and `<!-- END:nextjs-agent-rules -->` markers, and they're preserved when Next.js updates the managed block.
00082|
